note.title: Dystopian Literature — genre, conventions and change over time
note.overview: Recognise dystopian conventions, explain their effects, and compare how the genre can respond to different historical anxieties.
learningGoals: Analyse how a convention creates meaning.
Explain how context can shape genre concerns.
Recognise when a text challenges a convention.
mustMemoriseRules: Convention is not the same as rule: writers may adapt or subvert it.
Context should illuminate the text, not replace analysis.
A strong comparison states both similarity/difference and significance.
workedExamples: Surveillance can make private life impossible, increasing the sense of control and vulnerability.
A later text may shift an older fear into a new technological or social form.
commonMistakes: Treating every bleak setting as automatically dystopian.
Bolting on context without connecting it to the text.
detailedExplanation: The curriculum scope and assessed skills are verified against the official Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 English Curriculum Outline 2026-27.
Practice extracts and prompts in this bank are app-written unless explicitly identified otherwise. They are not copies of the teacher’s live assessment paper.
Long creative or essay responses are practice/self-check tasks and do not by themselves create formal Mastery evidence.
examTips: Keep a clear line of argument.
Move beyond feature-spotting: explain effect and significance.
Use focused textual references rather than retelling.
quickCheck: Analyse how a convention creates meaning.
Explain how context can shape genre concerns.
Recognise when a text challenges a convention.
beforeStartingPractice: Recall the core conventions or methods before opening notes.
